## What Lore does

Lore is an [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) that sits between Claude Code and your org's collective knowledge. It auto-detects which repo you're working in from the git remote and serves the right context. No manual loading.

The install takes about 30 seconds:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:[GITHUB-ORG]/lore.git && lore/scripts/install.sh
```

After install, Claude Code has access to MCP tools across three categories: **context** (org-wide CLAUDE.md, ADRs, hybrid search across all indexed content), **memory** (persistent store with semantic search, a live knowledge graph, and episode ingestion), and **pipeline** (delegate tasks to agents running on Kubernetes).

The context tools combine HNSW vector similarity with BM25 keyword matching via Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Early versions used vector-only search, which handled conceptual queries well ("how do we handle auth?") but missed exact matches on function names and config keys. Adding keyword search fixed this without complicating the API.

Memory changed how we work more than the context tools did. When an agent remembers that a particular approach failed yesterday, it stops repeating the mistake. Memories are versioned and searchable by semantic similarity. When running locally, memory operations proxy to the remote server so what one developer learns is available to everyone.

The original memory store was a flat key-value system. That worked for explicit "remember this" commands but missed the knowledge that accumulates passively: what came up in a PR review, what an agent tried and abandoned during a session, which services depend on each other. We added episode ingestion to capture that. `write_episode` accepts raw text and auto-extracts facts and knowledge graph entities from it. The review-reactor job now captures PR feedback as episodes automatically, and a Claude Code Stop hook captures session summaries at the end of every conversation.

Facts have temporal validity windows. When an agent stores something that contradicts an existing fact, the old one is invalidated via embedding similarity (threshold 0.92). You can query `search_memory` with `include_invalidated` to see the history of what the org believed and when it changed.

The extracted entities feed a live knowledge graph in PostgreSQL. `query_graph` lets agents ask about relationships, like which services talk to the auth library or which teams own what. `search_memory` can enrich results with 1-hop graph neighbors. `assemble_context` pulls from all sources and formats the result into a token-budgeted block using configurable YAML templates per task type (review, implementation, research).

None of this works if agents forget to use it. Sessions follow an enforced workflow: `assemble_context` runs first to load conventions, ADRs, memories, and graph context. `search_memory` runs before planning or building to check whether the problem was already solved. At session end, `write_memory` stores a summary and `write_episode` captures raw session content for passive fact extraction. The enforcement is what makes the knowledge accumulation automatic rather than opt-in.

**Score:** 1.000

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  # A new advisory lands on an unchanged tree, and the repository can go days without a push. Monday 07:00 UTC;
  # only build-chain answers it (#202).
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # Both re:cinq libraries install from the npm registry, whose tarballs ship
      # built code, so no dependency needs a lifecycle script.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # The api tests run against a real mongod, ~100MB that would otherwise be
      # downloaded again on every run. Keyed on the pinned version.
      - name: Cache the mongod the api tests start
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/mongodb-binaries
          key: mongod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('apps/api/test/mongoTestServer.ts') }}

      # A git or file dependency skips the registry the published libraries exist to prove (#13).
      - name: Keep dependency specifiers on the npm registry
        run: npm run check:dependencies

      # The engine's package root pulls every provider SDK into the browser, and booking data must never touch storage.
      # A test file ships in no bundle, so it may import the engine's recordedFrames; shipped code never does.
      - name: Keep HAL Engine and browser storage out of the web app
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine|import\(['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine" apps/web/src --exclude='*.test.ts' --exclude='*.test.tsx'; then
            echo "shipped apps/web code must not import @re-cinq/hal-engine" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if jq -e '.dependencies["@re-cinq/hal-engine"]' apps/web/package.json > /dev/null; then
            echo "apps/web may list @re-cinq/hal-engine under devDependencies only" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -rnE "localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|fetch\(|sendBeacon" apps/web/src/chat apps/web/src/screens apps/web/src/personas; then
            echo "apps/web chat code must not touch browser storage or send anything but the socket" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The model allowlist gates what configuration/ reads; a second reader would bypass it.
      - name: Read model, region and provider settings only in the api configuration
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "process\.env" apps packages --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
            | grep -E "MODEL|REGION|LOCATION|PROVIDER" | grep -v '^apps/api/src/configuration/'; then
            echo "only apps/api/src/configuration/ may read a model, region or provider value from process.env" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Declared twice, the band and the model's rule drift apart silently.
      - name: Keep the AI disclosure text in @support-agent/disclosure
        run: |
          if grep -rn "AI-assistent\|kunstig intelligens" apps/api/src apps/web/src; then
            echo "apps must import the AI disclosure from @support-agent/disclosure" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # example.com until KU-30 names the domain people who may read a conversation work at.
      - name: Keep human IAM bindings inside infra/terraform/access
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-deploy-invariants.ts infra/terraform --domain example.com

      # SC-002: the transport seam only holds if fetchTransport is the one way out; a second caller would skip deadline, retry and redaction.
      - name: Keep network access in the TMS client's transport.ts
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "\bfetch\(|['\"](node:)?(http|https|undici)['\"]" packages/tms-client/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v '^packages/tms-client/src/transport\.ts:'; then
            echo "only packages/tms-client/src/transport.ts may reference fetch, undici, http or https" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The reader prints whole conversations to an operator's terminal: never into a log, onto the network, or into the running service.
      # httpConversationHandler.ts is the deliberate HTTP-adapter exception to the import ban (SC-005/RD-13).
      - name: Keep the conversation reader offline and out of the running service
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"](node:)?(http|https|ws|express)['\"]|from ['\"][^'\"]*shared/logger" apps/api/src/reader --exclude="httpConversationHandler.ts"; then
            echo "apps/api/src/reader must not import the application logger, express, http, https or ws (httpConversationHandler.ts is exempt)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"][^'\"]*/reader/" apps/api/src/tools apps/api/src/escalation apps/api/src/start-server.ts; then
            echo "the running service must not reach apps/api/src/reader" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -nE "from ['\"](mongodb|[^'\"]*readConversation)" apps/api/src/reader/conversationView.ts; then
            echo "conversationView.ts must stay pure: no mongodb, no readConversation" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -nE "from ['\"]mongodb" apps/api/src/reader/httpConversationHandler.ts; then
            echo "httpConversationHandler.ts must not import mongodb" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # SC-004: a second timer would be one that shutdown does not clear.
      - name: Keep exactly one setInterval in the api, in shared/periodicJobs.ts
        run: |
          count=$(grep -rn "setInterval(" apps/api/src | wc -l)
          if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "apps/api/src must hold exactly one setInterval call, found $count; add a job to startPeriodicJobs instead" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Only a reader may reach a vendor; the diff, the CLI and the freshness check run on recorded values.
      - name: Keep vendor SDKs inside the drift readers
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "(from|import\() *['\"](@google-cloud/|@google/genai|@anthropic-ai/|openai|@aws-sdk/|@re-cinq/hal-engine)" \
            packages/control-drift scripts --include='*.ts' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
            | grep -v '^packages/control-drift/src/readers/'; then
            echo "only packages/control-drift/src/readers/ may import a vendor SDK" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # CR-005: every pull request, whether or not anyone ran the recorder.
      - name: Scan committed TMS fixtures for personal data and credentials
        run: |
          node packages/tms-client/scripts/scan-fixtures.mjs
          node packages/tms-client/scripts/scan-fixtures.mjs apps/api/stand-in-tms

      # Lore's lore_list_tests reads this output; an entry printing anything but {id, name, file} objects breaks it silently.
      - name: Check every Lore test-command list prints a JSON array of tests
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          file=.lore/test-commands.yml
          cwds=$(sed -n 's/^  cwd: //p' "$file")
          lists=$(sed -n 's/^  list: //p' "$file")
          if [ "$(echo "$cwds" | wc -l)" -ne "$(echo "$lists" | wc -l)" ]; then
            echo "$file: every entry needs exactly one cwd and one list" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          paste -d '\t' <(echo "$cwds") <(echo "$lists") | while IFS=$'\t' read -r cwd list; do
            echo "::group::$cwd: $list"
            (cd "$cwd" && bash -c "$list") > "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json"
            if ! jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; (.id | type) == "string" and (.name | type) == "string" and (.file | type) == "string")' "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json" > /dev/null; then
              echo "$cwd: '$list' did not print a non-empty JSON array of {id, name, file}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "$(jq length "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json") tests listed"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

      # The chat screen shows persona labels only; a persona's prompt prose or routing keywords in the bundle would publish the agent's instructions.
      - name: Keep persona prompt text out of the web bundle
        run: |
          node --input-type=module -e "
            const {PERSONA_REGISTRY} = await import('./apps/api/dist/prompt/personas.js');
            const prompts = Object.values(PERSONA_REGISTRY.personas).flatMap((persona) => [persona.overlay, ...persona.match]);
            console.log(['PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER', ...prompts].filter(Boolean).join('\\n'));
          " > "$RUNNER_TEMP/persona-prompt-text.txt"
          if grep -rnF -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/persona-prompt-text.txt" apps/web/dist; then
            echo "apps/web/dist must not contain a persona overlay, match keyword or PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # A tool registered without its Danish sentences must fail here, not render a gap.
      - name: Re-record the registered tool names and fail on drift
        run: |
          npm run record-tool-names -w @support-agent/api
          git diff --exit-code apps/web/src/chat/__fixtures__/tool-names.json

  browser:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Install Chromium
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
        working-directory: apps/web

      - name: Browser tests
        run: npm run test:browser

  # A stopped schedule looks like "nothing drifted"; only the age of the newest reading tells them apart.
  # A missing compliance-readings branch fails the second checkout: nothing has ever been read.
  reading-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          ref: compliance-readings
          path: compliance-readings
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Check the newest retention reading is under two schedule intervals old
        run: node scripts/check-reading-freshness.ts compliance-readings/observations/retention.jsonl

  chart:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@9bc31f4ebc9c6b171d7bfbaa5d006ae7abdb4310 # v5.0.1

      # kubeconform publishes no container image, only release tarballs.
      - name: Install kubeconform
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o kubeconform.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/yannh/kubeconform/releases/download/v0.8.0/kubeconform-linux-amd64.tar.gz
          echo "9bc2bffbf71f261128533edaf912153948b7ff238f9a531ae6d34466ec287883  kubeconform.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf kubeconform.tar.gz kubeconform
          rm kubeconform.tar.gz

      - name: Lint, render and validate the chart
        run: |
          helm lint charts/otto --strict -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            | ./kubeconform -strict -summary \
                -schema-location default \
                -schema-location 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datreeio/CRDs-catalog/main/{{.Group}}/{{.ResourceKind}}_{{.ResourceAPIVersion}}.json'

      # The api refuses to start without a database, so the chart must refuse to
      # render one that would never come up.
      - name: Refuse to render the api without its MongoDB settings
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '                  key: url'
          for setting in api.mongoSecretName api.mongoDbName; do
            if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
              --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set "$setting=" \
              --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml; then
              echo "an empty $setting must fail to render" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      # The retention period is a GDPR decision with no chart default, so the
      # chart must pass it through and refuse to render without one.
      - name: Render CONVERSATION_RETENTION_DAYS and refuse to render without api.conversationRetentionDays
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: CONVERSATION_RETENTION_DAYS' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "30"'
          if refusal=$(helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.conversationRetentionDays= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml 2>&1); then
            echo "an empty api.conversationRetentionDays must fail to render" >&2
            exit 1
          fi; grep -q 'api.conversationRetentionDays is required' <<<"$refusal"

      # Named, the api pod runs as the account Workload Identity binds; unset,
      # the field is absent and the pod falls back to the namespace default.
      - name: Render the api pod with and without api.serviceAccountName
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '      serviceAccountName: "otto-api"'
          if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.serviceAccountName= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml | grep -n "serviceAccountName:"; then
            echo "an empty api.serviceAccountName must render no serviceAccountName field" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Set, every tester is numbered from api.firstCustomerNumber and the login
      # Secret needs no customerNumbers key; unset, the pairs come from that key.
      - name: Render the api's customer numbers with and without api.firstCustomerNumber
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: LOGIN_FIRST_CUSTOMER_NUMBER' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "10001"'
          if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml | grep -n "key: customerNumbers"; then
            echo "api.firstCustomerNumber must leave the Secret's customerNumbers key unread" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.firstCustomerNumber= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '                  key: customerNumbers'

      # The api refuses to start without TMS_MODE, and live mode without its key,
      # so the chart refuses to render either; the key only ever comes from a Secret.
      - name: Render the api's TMS mode and refuse an incomplete one
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: TMS_MODE' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "stand-in"'
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.tmsMode=live \
            --set api.tmsBaseUrl=https://tms.example/api/ext/v1 --set api.tmsSecretName=otto-tms \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A4 -x '            - name: TMS_API_KEY' \
            | grep -qx '                  key: apiKey'
          for incomplete in "api.tmsMode=" "api.tmsMode=off" "api.tmsMode=on" "api.tmsMode=live"; do
            if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
              --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set "$incomplete" \
              --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "$incomplete must fail to render" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

  terraform:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@dfe3c3f87815947d99a8997f908cb6525fc44e9e # v4.0.1
        with:
          terraform_version: 1.16.2
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Check formatting
        run: terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform

      - name: Keep the compliance reader free of write and model-invoking roles
        run: |
          if grep -nE 'roles/[A-Za-z.]*(admin|editor|writer|user)"' infra/terraform/recinq-test/compliance-reader.tf; then
            echo "the compliance reader may hold no role ending in admin, editor, writer or user" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate every root
        run: |
          for root in infra/terraform/modules/otto-deployer infra/terraform/modules/otto-access-identity infra/terraform/modules/otto-runtime-identity infra/terraform/recinq-test infra/terraform/access; do
            terraform -chdir="$root" init -backend=false -input=false
            terraform -chdir="$root" validate
          done

      - name: Validate audit trail routing invariants
        run: ./audit.acceptance.test.sh
        working-directory: infra/terraform/access

  images:
    # No image is built or pushed over an unacknowledged high advisory or an unpinned action (#202).
    needs: [verify, chart, build-chain]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      matrix:
        component: [api, web]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631027851001ddb9b187196cc803df7f5f0e # v4.3.0

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}

## What is never written

- **GDPR data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(c).** No persisted document holds an `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `host` key at any depth, asserted by walking every key of the serialised document rather than checking its top-level fields — depth is the point rather than a flourish, since `ToolEntry.toolInput` is model-supplied data and a token can arrive nested inside a tool's input, so stripping only the top level would be theatre ([validated by: holds no credential key at any depth of the stored document](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L50)).

- Sanitising copies rather than mutates, because the live session keeps the credentials the orchestrator hands to tools through `ToolContext` ([validated by: leaves the caller their in-memory credentials, which the tools still need](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L82); a conversation reloaded in a fresh process therefore has no `authHeaders`, and a tool that reads them sees nothing until the caller re-authenticates, which is the intended trade-off and matches what the transport already does on socket close).

## What we learned

Early versions focused on serving CLAUDE.md and ADRs. That helped, but persistent memory was the bigger change. `search_memory` with semantic search over extracted facts gets called more than any tool except `get_context`. Static context tells the agent what the conventions are. Memory tells it what was tried, what failed, and what the team decided last week. The second kind of knowledge is harder to write down and more useful.

The 3rd party wrapper experience taught us that wrapping a black-box system and parsing its output is a losing strategy. Four attempts at output stripping, all failed. When we switched to direct API calls with structured output, the parsing problems went away.

After removing 3rd party wrapper and Beads, we had a list of eight gaps. We didn't rebuild all of them. Some capabilities, like CRDT sync and the original tree-sitter integration, turned out to be unnecessary for the workflows we actually ran. The system got simpler.

The memory search bug taught us that agent infrastructure needs the same observability as any production system. A clean log doesn't mean things are working. We added health checks and the `agent_stats` tool after that one. More recently we added persistent log storage. Every Job pod's output goes to GCS with a redaction pipeline that strips API keys, JWTs, and connection strings before storage. The web UI reads logs per-task with GitHub-based access control. When something goes wrong now, we can actually look at what happened.

## What is never written

- **GDPR data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(c).** No persisted document holds an `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `host` key at any depth, asserted by walking every key of the serialised document rather than checking its top-level fields — depth is the point rather than a flourish, since `ToolEntry.toolInput` is model-supplied data and a token can arrive nested inside a tool's input, so stripping only the top level would be theatre ([validated by: holds no credential key at any depth of the stored document](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L50)).
- The redaction removes credentials and nothing else, so the guarantee is not met by writing an empty document ([validated by: keeps everything that is not a credential, so the redaction is not simply emptying the document](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L57)).
- Sanitising copies rather than mutates, because the live session keeps the credentials the orchestrator hands to tools through `ToolContext` ([validated by: leaves the caller their in-memory credentials, which the tools still need](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L82); a conversation reloaded in a fresh process therefore has no `authHeaders`, and a tool that reads them sees nothing until the caller re-authenticates, which is the intended trade-off and matches what the transport already does on socket close).

## Redaction

- `redactEntry` rewrites a tool entry, and an entry a tool returns, before it is stored, so a policy that empties `toolInput` leaves the session holding no tool arguments ([validated by: rewrites a tool entry before it is stored, so the session holds no tool arguments](../../src/orchestration/entryMutations.test.ts#L116), [validated by: applies orchestrator.entries to the transport's writes: a redacted tool input stored and sent, the answer redacted at commit, and older entries cleared when the turn ends](../../src/historyControls.test.ts#L80), [validated by: redacts an entry a tool returns before it is stored, and yields the stored entry for the transport to send](../../src/historyControls.test.ts#L134)).
- An assistant or thinking entry is redacted once, when it is committed, and never while it is empty and streaming ([validated by: sees an answer once, when it is committed, and not while it is empty and streaming](../../src/orchestration/entryMutations.test.ts#L124), [validated by: applies orchestrator.entries to the transport's writes: a redacted tool input stored and sent, the answer redacted at commit, and older entries cleared when the turn ends](../../src/historyControls.test.ts#L80)).
- `redactEntry` never receives a user's entry ([validated by: never hands a user's own entry to redactEntry](../../src/orchestration/entryMutations.test.ts#L144)).
- A `redactEntry` that throws, or that returns an entry of another role, stores the entry cleared instead and logs one error naming only the entry's role ([validated by: stores the entry cleared and logs only its role when redactEntry returns another role](../../src/orchestration/entryMutations.test.ts#L152), [validated by: stores the entry cleared when redactEntry throws](../../src/orchestration/entryMutations.test.ts#L163)).

## What we learned

Early versions focused on serving CLAUDE.md and ADRs. That helped, but persistent memory was the bigger change. `search_memory` with semantic search over extracted facts gets called more than any tool except `get_context`. Static context tells the agent what the conventions are. Memory tells it what was tried, what failed, and what the team decided last week. The second kind of knowledge is harder to write down and more useful.

The 3rd party wrapper experience taught us that wrapping a black-box system and parsing its output is a losing strategy. Four attempts at output stripping, all failed. When we switched to direct API calls with structured output, the parsing problems went away.

After removing 3rd party wrapper and Beads, we had a list of eight gaps. We didn't rebuild all of them. Some capabilities, like CRDT sync and the original tree-sitter integration, turned out to be unnecessary for the workflows we actually ran. The system got simpler.

The memory search bug taught us that agent infrastructure needs the same observability as any production system. A clean log doesn't mean things are working. We added health checks and the `agent_stats` tool after that one. More recently we added persistent log storage. Every Job pod's output goes to GCS with a redaction pipeline that strips API keys, JWTs, and connection strings before storage. The web UI reads logs per-task with GitHub-based access control. When something goes wrong now, we can actually look at what happened.
